config.recorded: Recorded from the live site on 22 October 2026.

moments.title: Welcome to the tour
moments.text: This short tour of iLIT will walk through some of the key features of the website. Press Next to move along, Back to go back, or Exit at any time.

moments.title: Research
moments.text: Let's begin in the research tab.

moments.title: Search for a case
moments.text: This is the search bar, where research starts. We will begin with a simple search for a well known decision.

moments.title: Search results
moments.text: Search results display key information such as the citation, court, date, judge, outcome and how many decisions cite the case. Next, let's open some advanced search filters.

moments.title: Filters
moments.text: Filters are used in combination to narrow search results. Combine multiple selections to find specific case types. Clicking a filter will automatically search the library and display the results. Let's apply some filters: we will search for Refugee protection cases, won by the government, with the cessation and Sri Lanka tags.

moments.title: Filtered results
moments.text: We have 16 cases in the library that are classified as refugee protection, contain both the cessation and Sri Lanka tags, and were won by the government. Let's continue and open the top result, Veerasingam v. Canada.

moments.title: The reader
moments.text: This is the reader. It is comprised of three main sections, the header, the side panel, and the decision text.

moments.title: The decision
moments.text: The decision has been pulled from the FC Website, the text has been processed, and displayed in a formatted, easy to read way. iLIT marks what it has identified in the text with coloured highlights: case to case citations in gold, law and statute references in purple, and keyword tags in green. Let's continue, and see what a case to case citation looks like in the reader.

moments.title: Citations
moments.text: iLIT has connected every reference to its source in the database, meaning that users can see the text being referred to without leaving the site. Hovering over the yellow highlighted Camayo citation shows a text preview.

moments.title: Citation cards
moments.text: Each citation can be expanded out, and opened as a paragraph in the decision. The pin icon keeps it from disappearing, the i icon will provide more information in the side panel. Let's move on to the side panel next.

moments.title: The side panel: About
moments.text: The side panel has three main sections. The first section is called About. It sums up the case: the outcome, the decision maker, how many decisions cite it and what it cites, and the topics found in the text.

moments.title: The side panel: Authorities
moments.text: The Authorities tab groups and lists all citations and statutes that iLIT has identified within this decision. This can be used to navigate the decision.

moments.title: The side panel: Intelligence
moments.text: The final section of the side panel, Intelligence, has two subsections, Citation Intelligence, and Judge Profiles. Both default to the current case. Intelligence shows information from iLIT about how this case connects to others in the Library.

moments.title: The side panel: Judge Profiles
moments.text: The judge profile gives general insights into the decision maker for this decision.

moments.title: Next, Intelligence / Statistics
moments.text: Let's continue and open up the next main section of the website.

moments.title: Citation Intelligence
moments.text: This page is used to find the full citation intelligence features for decisions in the database. Let's return to a well known decision and search for Vavilov.

moments.title: Citation Intelligence
moments.text: This is the intelligence page for Vavilov.

moments.title: Citation Intelligence
moments.text: Scrolling down shows how often the case is cited each year, the outcomes in citing decisions, the courts and judges that cite it, and the statutes and authorities it travels with. Next, we continue to Judge Profiles.

moments.title: Judge Profiles
moments.text: This page provides a profile for each Judge identified in the database by iLIT.

moments.title: Finding a judge
moments.text: Typing a name narrows the list. Choosing the judge opens a profile snapshot: the number of decisions, how often the government and individuals succeeded, and the busiest year.

moments.title: Judge Profiles
moments.text: Scrolling down shows the decisions by year with their outcomes, the key decisions ranked by how many decisions cite them, and the types of matter. Next, we continue to the next section.

moments.title: Next, FC Activity
moments.text: Let's continue to the FC Activity intelligence tab.

moments.title: FC Activity Analytics
moments.text:
This next tab sets iLIT apart from any other available platform out there. Every other site is built upon published decisions. However, the vast majority of cases we work with never reach a final decision. This is a huge blind spot when we are trying to get an understanding of the litigation landscape.

iLIT contains the FC Activity information of every single IMM case ever filed in the Federal Court. This information was pulled and collected, and is valuable in that it can provide additional context and statistics that no other site can. The filters above will change the charts below.

moments.title: FC Activity Analytics
moments.text: Scrolling down shows more charts, including the outcomes by year filed, leave granted by decision under review, and the office that made the decision.

moments.title: Workbench
moments.text: Let's continue to the last major section of the website, the Analyst Workbench Demo.

moments.title: The Analyst Workbench
moments.text: This feature is still in development. It will serve as a personal log in page, allowing users to track their live IMM number cases, pin case law decisions, and much more. You are now signed in to a demo account.

moments.title: Live Analysis
moments.text: Finally, we will finish off by exploring the most impactful use case for iLIT - the Live Analysis Feature.

moments.title: Live Analysis
moments.text:
There are two important things to clarify before we continue.

1. iLIT today was built with the assistance of AI, but it does not run on it. The site works without relying on any external AI providers or third-party companies.

2. iLIT works by inputting plain text. What this means in practice is that **iLIT will work not just on court decisions, but on any inputted text.**

What this means is that iLIT can be used not just as a research tool for public decisions, but it can be used on any word document, or clearly legible PDF. And it can do it live, on the page, without storing anything permanently.

moments.title: A Word file, dropped in
moments.text: Let's demonstrate this functionality. We will drop in a made up word document and iLIT will process it, just like it has processed the 75k decisions in the database. The difference is, this process happens live, in memory, and the document is never saved by iLIT.

moments.title: A Word file, dropped in
moments.text: This is a fictional Memorandum of Argument from a refugee cessation judicial review, written for this demonstration. In practice it could be the memo filed by opposing counsel, or a draft an analyst is preparing.

moments.title: The memo, marked up
moments.text: iLIT went through the memo line by line. The counts show the case citations and statute references it found. Each one is marked in the text, as in the reader, so it can be previewed, opened as a card and pinned. A citation to a case in the library, such as Baker, links to that decision. This draft is not stored in the library, or added to the database in any way.

moments.title: That is the tour
moments.text: iLIT searches and reads Federal Court, Federal Court of Appeal and Supreme Court decisions, maps how they cite each other, profiles the judges, adds Federal Court activity data, and reads your own documents without saving them. The Workbench is still being built. Check out the 'see what is coming' section, or spend more time using the site.
